key_insight: For linear-elastic homogenization, stress is a one-local quantum observable obtainable from the same computational-basis measurements as the two-local equilibrium Hamiltonian.
engineering_relevance: The formulation extracts effective RVE stress for macroscale constitutive calculations without reconstructing the microscopic displacement field or adding a measurement basis.
method: Encode the reduced finite-element RVE energy as a QUBO and map it to an Ising Hamiltonian.
Approximate the equilibrium ground state using the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE).
Differentiate the strain-dependent Hamiltonian via Hellmann–Feynman to obtain stress observables containing only identity and single-qubit Pauli-Z terms.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a demonstration on a two-dimensional periodic RVE and establishes equivalence to conventional volume-averaged stress, but gives no quantitative accuracy or runtime results.
watch_item: Practical stress accuracy depends on the encoding resolution and VQE state quality; computational advantage is not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Ising-Encoded Computational Homogenization: Stress as a Quantum Observable
